commit.subject: fix(ledger): only count git commit in command position

entries.text: okay, in separate branch implement that. I want you to be able to use that action viewer for that PR that you will do with that feature. My idea is to be able to see agent's actions for each commit basically.

I'm trying to figure out where the viewer build work went relative to compaction, tracing commit actions by sha to pin down which one corresponds to the docs commit versus earlier ledger-sync work.

Looking at 92b9909 more closely, I realize my naive text search for "git commit" is catching false positives — a python heredoc that just mentions "`git commit` actions" in its text is being miscounted as an actual commit command, which explains the miscounted single action. I need a better heuristic that only matches git commit when it appears as an actual shell command, not just referenced in a string or comment.



The second commit now matches by SHA. I also spotted a false positive where commands just mentioning "git commit" in text were wrongly counted as commit actions, so I'll fix this by requiring `git` to appear in command position.

cd . && python3 - <<'EOF'
p="src/core/ledger.ts"; s=open(p).read()
a='const GIT_COMMIT = /\\bgit\\b(?:\\s+-[cC]\\s+\\S+)*\\s+commit\\b/;'
assert a in s
s=s.replace(a,'''// `git` in command position (start, or after `&&`, `;`, `|`, `(`, a newline, env assignments), so
// heredocs, greps and messages that merely mention "git commit" don't count.
const GIT_COMMIT = /(?:^|[;&|(\\n])\\s*(?:\\w+=\\S*\\s+)*git(?:\\s+-[cC]\\s+\\S+)*\\s+commit\\b/;''')
open(p,"w").write(s)
p="src/core/ledger.test.ts"; s=open(p).read()
a='''  user("u2", "2026-01-01T10:04:00Z"),'''
s=s.replace(a,a+'''
  action("grep", "2026-01-01T10:04:10Z", "rg 'git commit' src && cat <<EOF\\n/** `git commit` */\\nEOF"),''')
open(p,"w").write(s)
EOF
